title: Jharkhand's rural job scheme and tap-water mission: what the audit record shows and leaves open
dek: An audit of two public programmes in Jharkhand examines how funds moved and how work was recorded, but it does not settle what the people who depend on these schemes experienced on the ground.
indiaConnection: This audit examines how a public programme in Jharkhand was carried out and recorded, and it states what the audited record can and cannot establish for the people in India who depend on it.

eventTime.label: Date not established in the supplied evidence

body.text: Rural households in Jharkhand depend on two national programmes for wage employment and drinking water. The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme promises at least 100 days of paid unskilled work per year to every rural household that volunteers. The Jal Jeevan Mission aims to give each rural household a functional tap connection for safe water. The audit record examined here looks at how these schemes were implemented in the state between 2019 and 2024.

The audit covered the employment scheme by checking records at the state commissioner's office, six districts, twelve blocks, and forty-eight gram panchayats. It also physically verified 480 selected works and surveyed beneficiaries. For the water mission, the audit examined records from 2019-20 to 2023-24, focusing on planning, implementation, and sustainability of assets. The record does not include independent measurements of water quality or employment outcomes beyond what the audit itself observed.

The employment scheme is administered by the MGNREGA Commissioner in Jharkhand, with district, block, and gram panchayat offices responsible for implementation. The audit examined the planning process, the allocation and use of funds, and the monitoring and grievance redressal systems. The record shows that the scheme's design requires these layers to work together, but it does not say how effectively they did so in practice.

For the water mission, the State Water and Sanitation Mission led implementation with support from district missions and village committees. The Drinking Water and Sanitation Department of the state government was the nodal department. The audit assessed whether the institutional framework was efficient and whether financial resources were used economically. The record does not establish whether the village committees had the capacity to manage the systems after installation.

The review considered how money was assigned, given out, and spent for the job program. It also checked if the facilities built under the water initiative would last for the coming twenty to thirty years. The record gives information on money movement and facility building, but it doesn't link these to the real count of workdays offered or the number of homes that received water connections.

section.title: What the record shows about funds and assets

body.text: The audit's findings are based on test-checked records and physical verification of a sample of works. This means the record can show patterns in the sampled offices and sites, but it cannot say what happened in the many other gram panchayats and villages not covered. The record does not include data on whether the water assets continued to function after the audit period.

The audit record is an independent examination of the institutions' own records. It can contradict or narrow the official account, but it does not include independent reporting or measurement from outside the audit. There is no evidence from people directly affected by the schemes about whether they received the promised work or water. The record also does not test the issuing institution's account with external data.

section.title: What is missing from the record

body.text: For the employment scheme, the audit surveyed beneficiaries, but the record does not say what those surveys found. For the water mission, the audit assessed whether assets were sustainable, but it does not provide evidence on the quality of water delivered. These gaps mean the record cannot settle what the schemes actually achieved for rural households in Jharkhand.

statements.text: The 2005 National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, which was renamed in 2009, promises a minimum of 100 days of paid work each year to rural families willing to perform manual labor that doesn't require skills.
statements.sourceScope: The audit report's description of the legal mandate of the employment scheme.
statements.limits: The record does not state how many households actually received the guaranteed days of work in Jharkhand.

statements.text: In August 2019, the Jal Jeevan Mission started with the goal of delivering adequate and clean drinking water to every rural home via functional taps by 2024.
statements.sourceScope: The audit report's description of the water mission's objective and launch.
statements.limits: The record does not state how many households in Jharkhand received functional tap connections by the end of 2024.

statements.text: The audit of the employment scheme covered the period 2019-24 and test-checked records at the state commissioner's office, six districts, twelve blocks, and forty-eight gram panchayats.
statements.sourceScope: The audit report's description of the scope of the performance audit of the employment scheme.
statements.limits: The record does not say what happened in the many gram panchayats not included in the test-checked sample.

statements.text: The water mission's audit took place between September and November 2024, covering the years 2019-20 to 2023-24.
statements.sourceScope: The audit report's description of the period and timing of the water mission audit.
statements.limits: The record does not include any data from after November 2024, so it cannot say whether the mission met its 2024 target.

statements.text: The employment scheme is implemented by the MGNREGA Commissioner in Jharkhand, with district, block, and gram panchayat offices responsible for execution.
statements.sourceScope: The audit report's description of the administrative structure for the employment scheme.
statements.limits: The record does not assess the performance of individual offices or staff.

statements.text: The State Water and Sanitation Mission led implementation of the water mission in Jharkhand, with support from district missions and village committees.
statements.sourceScope: The audit report's description of the institutional framework for the water mission.
statements.limits: The record does not state whether the village committees had the resources or training to manage the systems.

statements.text: The Drinking Water and Sanitation Department of the Government of Jharkhand was the nodal department for the water mission.
statements.sourceScope: The audit report's description of the nodal department for the water mission.
statements.limits: The record does not detail the department's specific actions or decisions.

statements.text: The review looked at how money was earmarked, distributed, and spent for the employment program.
statements.sourceScope: The audit report's description of the financial aspects covered in the employment scheme audit.
statements.limits: The record does not state whether the funds reached the intended beneficiaries.

statements.text: The audit checked if the facilities built under the water mission would remain usable for the next twenty to thirty years.
statements.sourceScope: The audit report's description of the sustainability assessment for water mission assets.
statements.limits: The record does not provide evidence on the actual condition of the assets after the audit period.

statements.text: The audit physically verified 480 selected works and surveyed beneficiaries of the employment scheme.
statements.sourceScope: The audit report's description of the physical verification and beneficiary survey for the employment scheme.
statements.limits: The record does not include the results of the beneficiary survey or the physical verification findings.

statements.text: The audit record is an independent examination of the institutions' own records, but it does not include independent reporting or measurement from outside the audit.
statements.sourceScope: The audit report's role as an independent audit of institutional records.
statements.limits: The record does not contain any external data or independent verification beyond the audit's own checks.

statements.text: The record does not establish what the schemes actually achieved for rural households, such as the number of days of work provided or the quality of water delivered.
statements.sourceScope: The audit report's coverage of the employment scheme and water mission implementation.
statements.limits: The record does not answer whether the schemes met their objectives for the people who depend on them.

perspectives.label: Audit perspective
perspectives.rationale: The audit is the only source in the dossier, and it provides an independent examination of the schemes' implementation.
perspectives.sees: The audit sees the schemes through the lens of official records and its own physical verification.
perspectives.values: It values accountability and efficiency in the use of public funds.
perspectives.uses: It uses test-checked records and sample surveys to draw conclusions about the schemes.
perspectives.mayMiss: It may miss the actual experiences of beneficiaries and the quality of water or work on the ground.
